2.8.status_note: `shipped-and-validated` — root cause reproduced and confirmed 2026-07-24 (console-driven repro against the live Docker dev server, not just static reading): a melee hit's `onMeleeHit` callback can synchronously drop the player to 0 HP mid-iteration of `updateEnemies`'s `for` loop; `handleDeath()` then destroys **every** enemy (including ones the loop hasn't reached yet) and reassigns `this.enemies`, so the loop's next iteration calls `.update()` on an already-destroyed enemy whose Arcade `body` Phaser has nulled — throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'setVelocity')`, an uncaught exception inside Phaser's step that freezes the game. Fixed in `src/scenes/SpellroadScene.ts`'s `updateEnemies`: snapshot the array before iterating (`[...this.enemies]`, matching the pattern `confirmCast` already uses for the same reason) and skip any enemy whose `.active` is now `false`. Verified: re-ran the identical repro post-fix (no throw, HP/enemies reset correctly) and a normal no-death multi-enemy tick (both enemies stay `active`, unaffected). `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` clean post-fix.

2.18.status_note: `shipped-and-validated` (investigation, not a fix — none was needed) — traced `SpellCaster.buildHitTest` and `SpellroadScene.confirmCast`'s hit loop by hand against a concrete scenario (3 clustered enemies, a caster, and an aim direction) rather than assuming a bug or assuming it's fine: line and cone both correctly returned `true` for all 3 clustered enemies simultaneously — the loop applies damage to every enemy the shape's `hitTest` accepts, up to `maxTargets`, with no cap-at-one logic anywhere. Circle behaves differently by design (it's a placement spell — the hit area is centered on the aimed *point*, not the caster — see Warden/Heckler's 2026-07-25 framing, "zone-denial via placement, not a target lock"); aiming loosely toward a cluster instead of directly onto it will legitimately whiff some or all of it. Most likely explanation for what the developer saw: (a) two of the default loadout's line spells (`stone_spike`, `magma_lance`) are deliberately single-target (`base_targets: 1`) by design, not a bug; (b) real enemies move independently and rarely stay clustered within the line shape's narrow ±13px width or a cone's exact facing at the same instant the way a hand-picked test scenario does; (c) circle specifically needs the placement reticle aimed directly onto the cluster. Asked the developer to re-test watching the shape preview before confirming a cast, aimed squarely over 2+ visibly clustered enemies, and report back if it still only ever hits one — that would be a real, reproducible signal worth a deeper live-repro dive, which hand-tracing the algorithm can't substitute for.

4.11.status_note: `shipped-and-validated` — GitHub issue #97, closed 2026-08-06 on the developer merging PR #99. **Real gap found before this could be "just wiring":** the only shipped asset was a raw `.mid` — Phaser's sound manager can't play raw MIDI in a browser (no bundled synth), so the ticket as filed was one step short of buildable. Developer's call (2026-08-05 check-in): render it to real audio in an isolated scratch venv rather than install system audio tooling (fluidsynth/ffmpeg) on the host. Rendered via `pretty_midi.synthesize()` (naive additive sine-wave synthesis, no soundfont/system dependency) and written straight to Ogg Vorbis via `soundfile` (its pip wheel bundles libsndfile with Vorbis support, so no `ffmpeg` call needed either) — `public/assets/audio/music/boss-1-invigilator-trial-theme.ogg` (130KB, 60s, all 4 instruments present). **Standing disclosed limitation, carried forward past this closure, not resolved by it:** the synthesized quality is a plain sine-wave approximation, not the real cello/harp/pad/bells timbre Composer's `.mid` specifies — same handling as other disclosed tradeoffs in this backlog (0.6/3.10). The merge covers "does it play, loop, and stop correctly" (the wiring this ticket actually scoped); it is not a developer sign-off that the audio quality itself is final — re-open or file a fresh ticket if a real soundfont/DAW render is wanted later.
